reason: E1 reports that tensile-compression asymmetry increases with Cu content and temperature, but it does not mention deformation twinning, wear, or any shift in deformation mechanism. The key premises linking Cu content to twinning, strain localization, and wear resistance are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: FeNiCrCoCu HEA exhibits tensile-compression asymmetry that increases with temperature and Cu content
Deformation twinning is a dominant mechanism in the baseline alloy at high temperature
Twinning leads to localized strain concentrations and higher wear
Reducing Cu content will shift deformation from twinning to dislocation slip
A shift to dislocation slip will improve wear resistance
